title: Regret-Based Federated Causal Discovery with Unknown Interventions
claim: Interventions on a node break symmetries in the equivalence class, letting undirected edges be oriented that observational data leaves ambiguous.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, colored boxes with (a)(b)(c) labels
description: Three small three-node graphs on nodes A, B, and C, shown side by side with (a), (b), (c) labels underneath. Panel (a) is the true DAG on a white background: A→C, B→C, and A→B, drawn as bold black arrows. Panel (b) sits in a pink rounded box. It shows the client CPDAG with no interventions, where all three edges are undirected, giving a triangle. The title above is C(G_Φ1); Φ1 = ∅. Panel (c) sits in a blue rounded box. It shows the CPDAG after node B is intervened on. A→C and B→C are directed, and the A–B edge is removed. The title above is C(G_Φ2); Φ2 = {B}. The eye goes first to the colored boxes, then to the contrast between the undirected triangle and the directed V-structure.
caption: (a) True causal DAG; (b) Client CPDAG with no interventions; (c) Client CPDAG of structurally intervened DAG.
abstract: Most causal discovery methods recover a completed partially directed acyclic graph representing a Markov equivalence class from observational data. Recent work has extended these methods to federated settings to address data decentralization and privacy constraints, but often under idealized assumptions that all clients share the same causal model. Such assumptions are unrealistic in practice, as client-specific policies or protocols, for example, across hospitals, naturally induce heterogeneous and unknown interventions. In this work, we address federated causal discovery under unknown client-level interventions. We propose I-PERI, a novel federated algorithm that first recovers the CPDAG of the union of client graphs and then orients additional edges by exploiting structural differences induced by interventions across clients. This yields a tighter equivalence class, which we call the $\mathbfÎ¦$-Markov Equivalence Class, represented by the $\mathbfÎ¦$-CPDAG. We provide theoretical guarantees on the convergence of I-PERI, as well as on its privacy-preserving properties, and present empirical evaluations on synthetic data demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.
